issues.legal_issue: A Hindu deity falls within the meaning of “individual” for assessment under the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922.
material_facts: Property had been dedicated to a Hindu deity and the dedication was held to be valid.
The deity was capable of holding the dedicated property and receiving income from it, and of suing and being sued.
The income of the debutter estate was assessed through the Official Trustee, who possessed and managed the property.
issues.conclusion: A Hindu deity is an “individual” within section 3 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, and can be treated as a unit of assessment; its income is assessed through the shebaits managing its property.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 3 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, “individual” includes a Hindu deity that is a juristic person capable of holding property and receiving income. The Court followed Jogendra Nath Naskar v. Commissioner of Income-tax (1969) 74 ITR 33 and relied on Commissioner of Income-tax v. Sodra Devi (32 ITR 615) for the breadth of “individual,” alongside the established authorities recognizing a Hindu deity as a juristic person, including Pramatha Nath Mullick v. Pradyumna Kumar Mullick (1925) LR 52 IA 245. The statutory language can encompass the deity without being strained, and assessment is made through the shebaits in possession and management of its property.

rule.if: income_tax_assessment_dispute and hindu_deity_is_juristic_person and deity_can_hold_property and deity_can_receive_income and deity_can_sue_or_be_sued

predicates.income_tax_assessment_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether income associated with a Hindu religious endowment is assessable as income-tax.
predicates.hindu_deity_is_juristic_person: The religious endowment is dedicated to a Hindu deity recognized as a juristic person.
predicates.deity_can_hold_property: The deity is capable of holding the property associated with the endowment.
predicates.deity_can_receive_income: The deity is capable of receiving income from its property.
predicates.deity_can_sue_or_be_sued: The deity has the capacity to sue and be sued in court.

issues.definition: When an income-tax assessment dispute concerns a juristic Hindu deity that can hold property, receive income, and sue or be sued, the deity is assessable as an individual.
